test.name: Fans out one search-records agent per open plan item
test.description: Issue #4441. On a job, research/SKILL.md's search step dispatches one search agent per open item of the active plan, as parallel calls in one message. Uses search-continue-authorized-in-message unmodified: one in_progress question q_001, active plan pl_001 with pli_001 (census) and pli_002 (church), both planned with no fallback_for, no log entries or assertions. The message is a job ('finding a record' alone would be a bounded ask that runs one search). The router must spawn search-records twice, each handed exactly one plan item and neither carrying the researcher's words. search-records is stubbed with the usual stop reply, so a dispatch that sends the two one after the other records one spawn and fails.

input.user_message: Keep researching this project. Work through whatever is still planned, and don't check in with me between searches.

judge_context: This is a ROUTING test. Whether search-records is reached, how many times it is spawned and what each spawn carries are asserted deterministically by validators that read the PreToolUse hook records (test_routes_to_expected_skill, test_delegation_hands_plan_item_verbatim, test_search_spawns_cover_each_open_item). You cannot see those records. Do NOT score Correctness or Completeness on which callee was reached, how many spawns there were, or the order of skills_invoked.

The project's active plan has two planned items (pli_001 census, pli_002 church) and no evidence yet. The researcher asked for the open searches to run without check-ins, so dispatching both in one step is correct.

search-records is STUBBED: each spawn returns "Your delegation is recorded and counts as complete" and runs no search. So saying both searches were handed off, delegated or dispatched is ACCURATE and is NOT a fabricated claim; no search results and no project changes are the expected state. Do not score Correctness or Completeness down for the missing results. Grade only the router's own work: whether it claims records were found or facts learned (that would be fabrication), and whether its state derivation is sound. A scratch run graded Correctness 1 three times for reading the hand-off as false, while every deterministic validator passed.
